hook.line: How to turn Claude Code into a team of six developers in five minutes.
hook.visual: Presenter in the top half by a bookshelf, a plugin web page in the bottom half, one big caption word on the seam; a light streak sweeps the screen.

beats.what: Promise spoken straight to camera: a six-developer team in five minutes, captions on the face/screen seam.
Item 1 (superpowers): GitHub repo card with the star count, then a pixel-art 'CLAUDE SUPERPOWERS PLUGIN' badge with a block robot.
Terminal install command typed in the lower half while he explains planning and tests.
Item 2 (front-end design): install count as a big caption number over the plugin's landing page.
Item 3 (code review): git log and blame shown in the terminal while he lists the parallel agents.
Item 4 (security review) introduced full-frame on his face with an italic serif title; zoom punch at 31.4 s.
Full-frame cutaway: a giant serif '5' on white with palm-leaf shadows marks item 5 (memory plugin).
'Recalled context' list in the terminal shows what memory keeps across sessions.
Item 6: plugin installed successfully, then a CEO-review agent output for a sample product.
Back to his face full frame with the comment keyword 'PLUGINS' in big italic type.

characters.who: Pixel-art block robot on the 'CLAUDE SUPERPOWERS' plugin badge
characters.enters: Appears in the lower screen half as a static badge when item 1 is named
characters.acts: Sits beside the pixel-type plugin name as its logo; an arrow points to the word 'plugin'
characters.exits: Cut away to the terminal on the next shot

why_it_works: Numbered list of six with a concrete count per item (stars, installs), so viewers stay to collect all six and know how far along they are.
Face fixed in the top half for 94% of the video while the bottom half changes about every second (median shot 0.97 s), so the eye always has something new without losing the speaker.
Comment-keyword CTA ('comment PLUGINS') promises the full list with links, which turns the list into a reason to comment.
A full-frame number card ('5') breaks the split layout once, resetting attention late in the list.
weaknesses: Screen recordings are small and dense (about 30 words on screen at once); the code is unreadable at phone size.
Six items in 54 s means each gets about one sentence, so it reads as a list to save, not to learn from.
78% of the on-screen text sits outside the safe area, so some of it collides with TikTok UI.
for_robert: Borrow the one-off full-frame number card (the big '5') as a chapter break, and let Fred hold up or swim past the number instead of a static card.
